meaning: 'While / during': the main action goes on for the whole stretch of time. Attaches to Verb-ている, an adjective, or noun + の.
'While / during', but the main action happens at one point inside that stretch instead of filling all of it (which is plain 間). Same attachments as 間.
With a negative verb or adjective: 'not very / not much'. A soft, partial negative, not a total denial.
'After': Verb-た form or noun + の + あとで. The main action follows once the first one is over.
Conditional 'if': verbs change the final -u to -eba (行けば), i-adjectives take -ければ. Sets a condition and the result that follows; common for general truths and hypotheticals.
'In the case of / if it happens that', for situations that may come up, typical of rules and instructions. Plain form, noun + の, or na-adjective + な.
Noun + ばかり: 'nothing but / only that', usually hinting there is too much of one thing (eats only meat, nothing but complaints).
'Just by / with only': one small thing on its own is enough to bring the result (just thinking about it is fun). Plain verb or noun + だけで.
Verb stem + 出す: something starts suddenly or bursts out, 'break into / start to' (burst out crying, suddenly started raining).
A very polite です, used by staff to customers and in formal announcements. Replaces です after nouns and na-adjectives.
Noun + でも: 'even' (even a child knows that), or a soft 'or something' in offers (coffee or something?). Not ても, which follows a verb's て form, and not the 'but' that opens a sentence.
Formal or written 'isn't it? / surely': presents something as obvious and invites agreement, or a surprised 'why, it's ...!'. The stiff counterpart of じゃないか.
Noun + が必要だ: '~ is needed'. Names the thing required; the person or purpose takes に or には.
Noun + がする for something you sense: a smell, sound, taste or feeling is noticed (it smells good, I hear a noise, I have a feeling).
Adjective stem + がり (often + 屋): a noun for someone who easily feels that way, like 'someone who's always cold' or 'a scaredy-cat'. A light, slightly teasing label.
Adjective stem (or たい stem) + がる: describes someone else's feelings or wishes from how they act ('acts scared', 'seems to want'). ている form for the current state.
A very polite あります, 'there is / we have', used in service and formal speech (the restroom is over there). Different from でございます, which replaces です.
Verb stem + 始める: 'start to / begin doing'. A neutral beginning of an action or change; compare 出す, which is sudden.
'Should be / is supposed to': a confident conclusion from facts or reasoning. Plain form, noun + の, or na-adjective + な.
'There's no way that / it can't be': the speaker reasons that something is impossible. The firm opposite of はずだ.
Dictionary form + 必要がある: 'need to / it's necessary to do'. 必要はない means 'there's no need to'. Takes a verb, while が必要 takes a noun.
Volitional form: godan verbs change -u to -ou (行こう), ichidan verbs swap る for よう (食べよう), する becomes しよう. Means 'let's' or 'I'll'; the polite version is ましょう.
Honorific verb for いる, 行く and 来る, used for the listener or someone you respect. Polite form is いらっしゃいます.
Humble polite form of します, for your own actions toward a customer or superior. Often in お / ご + verb + いたします.
Casual 'isn't it? / come on': insists something is obvious, scolds, or shows surprise ('hey, it's you!'). Sounds blunt and a bit masculine; ではないか is the formal version.
'Whether or not', for an embedded yes-no question: plain form + かどうか + know, ask, decide. Nouns and na-adjectives drop だ.
Sentence-final 'I wonder', soft and traditionally feminine. Does the same job as かな.
Casual ending for yes-no questions, warm or a little old-fashioned, mostly from male or older speakers. Plain form + かい.
'Might / may': possible but not certain. Plain form; nouns and na-adjectives drop だ. Polite: かもしれません.
Sentence-final 'I wonder', thinking aloud or softening a question. Casual and used by everyone, while かしら sounds feminine.
'Made from': the raw material is changed and can't be seen in the result (wine from grapes). With で作る the material is still visible.
'Surely / I bet': strong confidence in a guess or wish, often with だろう or と思う. Surer than たぶん.
'Around / about' a time. ごろ follows a clock time or date (around 3 o'clock); ころ follows a phrase or noun + の for a period (back when I was a child).
Plain verb + こと: turns a verb or clause into a noun, 'doing / the act of', so it can be a subject or object. The base of ことができる, ことがある and more.
Dictionary or ない form + ことがある: 'there are times when / sometimes'. Not たことがある with past た, which means 'have done before'.
Dictionary form + ことができる: 'can / be able to'. A bit more formal than the potential form; also for what's allowed (you can pay by card).
Dictionary or ない form + ことになる: 'it's been decided / it turns out that', when others or circumstances decide. ことにする is your own decision.
Dictionary or ない form + ことにする: 'decide to', a choice the speaker makes. ことにしている is a rule you keep for yourself.
I-adjective stem + くする: 'make something (more) ~' on purpose (make the room warmer, make it shorter). Na-adjectives and nouns use にする.
'Suddenly / all of a sudden', for an abrupt, unexpected change (it suddenly got cold, stopped without warning).
'By' a deadline: the action happens at some point before then. まで alone means 'until', the action lasting up to that time.
'As it is / unchanged': a state stays the same while something else happens (slept with the light on). Verb-た, ない form, noun + の, or adjective.
Formal 'or' between choices in notices, forms and instructions. In speech, か or それとも is more usual.
Casual 'seems / looks like': a guess from what you see or hear, or a comparison (it's like a dream). Plain form or noun directly, no の needed.
〜みたいな + noun: 'a [thing] like ~', describing or giving an example (a person like you). The adjective form of みたいだ.
〜みたいに + verb or adjective: 'like / as if', describing how something is done (sings like a pro). The adverb form of みたいだ.
Number + counter + も: 'as many as / as much as', stressing that the amount feels large (waited three whole hours). With a negative, 一つも〜ない is 'not even one'.
Dictionary form + な: a blunt 'don't!'. Rough and mostly male; seen on signs and in strong warnings. Much harsher than ないで.
'And so on / such as': picks examples from a longer list, or softens a single example. More formal than とか.
Verb stem + ながら: 'while doing', two actions by the same person at once. The main action comes last (study while listening to music).
With a negative: 'not easily / just won't', something takes longer or is harder than hoped (the bus just won't come).
ない form, drop い, add ければいけない: 'must / have to'. Leans toward personal or situational need; common in speech. Casual: なきゃ.
Also 'must / have to', but more formal and objective: rules, duties, social obligation and writing. いけない is the more personal, spoken version.
'If / if that's the case': picks up a topic or what someone just said and responds or advises (if it's sushi you want, go to ...). Plain form or noun.
Verb stem + なさい: a firm command from a parent, teacher or test paper (go to bed, choose one). Polite in shape but used toward people below you.
Honorific verb for する, used for what someone you respect does. Polite form なさいます; also ご + noun + なさる.
'Notice / realize': noun + に気がつく, or plain form + ことに気がつく. Something comes to your attention.
'Looks / appears (to be)': noun or na-adjective + に見える; i-adjectives take く見える. A judgement from how it looks.
Na-adjective or noun + にする: 'make something ~', changing its state on purpose (keep it quiet, make the room clean). The partner of くする, not the N5 'decide on' にする.
Verb stem + にくい: 'hard to do', because of the thing's nature (hard to read, hard to open). Opposite of やすい.
Noun + の中で: 'among / within' a group or range, setting the scope for a comparison or choice. Works with any statement, not only 一番.
'Although / even though', with surprise, frustration or regret that things went against expectations. Plain form; nouns and na-adjectives take な.
Dictionary form + のに: 'for / in order to', followed by words like 使う, 必要, 便利 or 時間がかかる. A purpose, unlike the 'although' のに.
'The one that ~ is X': plain form + のは moves information to the front so the part after it gets the focus (it was yesterday that I met him).

pattern: お〜ください / ご〜ください
meaning: お + verb stem (ご + suru-noun) + ください: a polite, respectful request (please wait). Softer and more formal than てください.

pattern: お〜になる / ご〜になる
meaning: お + verb stem + になる: honorific form for actions of someone you respect (the president has gone home). Verbs with their own honorific (いる, 見る, 言う) use that instead.
Number + counter + おきに: 'every other / at intervals of'. 一日おきに is every other day; with distances it gives the gap (trees every five meters).
Verb stem + 終わる: 'finish doing' (finish reading, finish eating).
Potential form, 'can do': ichidan verbs take られる (食べられる), godan verbs change -u to -eru (行ける). Same shape as the passive and honorific られる, so context decides.
'Seems / apparently': a conclusion from what you heard or read. Also noun + らしい for 'typical of / a proper ~' (very like him). Plain form; nouns attach directly.
Adjective stem + さ: turns an adjective into a noun for its degree, like '-ness' (height, the cold, kindness). Works with i- and na-adjectives.
'A moment ago / just now', casual. Points back a little while earlier.
Causative-passive: 'be made to do' something you didn't want (was made to wait). Godan verbs not ending in す often shorten to される (待たされる).
Causative, 'make or let someone do': ichidan + させる, godan -u to -aseru (行かせる), する to させる. The person doing it takes に or を.
Causative て form + ください: 'please let me do', asking permission or politely offering to do something.
Praise when someone or something lives up to its reputation: 'just what you'd expect from ~'. Often さすが + noun + だ.
Plain form + し: lists reasons or points, 'and what's more', often hinting there are others. Frequently the reasons behind a decision.
'That much / so', about a degree just mentioned. With a negative: 'not that ~ (not as much as you'd think)'.
'Even so / nevertheless': what follows holds despite what was just said.
'Besides / on top of that': adds one more point, often another reason, to what came before.
Hearsay: full plain form + そうだ, 'I heard that / they say', passing on information from a source. Unlike the 'looks like' そうだ, it follows the whole word (降るそうだ).
Appearance: verb stem or adjective stem + そうだ, a guess from how things look (looks tasty, it's about to rain). いい becomes よさそう. Not the hearsay そうだ.
Forms of the 'looks like' そうだ: そうな + noun (a tasty-looking cake), そうに + verb (smiling happily). Built on verb or adjective stems.
Verb-た + ばかり: 'just did', when it feels recent to the speaker even if some time has passed (I only started last month). たところ is literally moments ago.
Verb-た + ところ: 'have just done', the action finished a moment ago (I've just got home). Narrower and more literal than たばかり.

pattern: 〜を開ける / 〜が開く (他動詞・自動詞)
meaning: Transitive verbs take を and someone does the action (I open the door); intransitive verbs take が and the thing happens by itself (the door opens). Many come in pairs.
Verb stem + たがる: 'wants to do' for someone else, judged from their behavior; usually たがっている. たい is only for the speaker.
Past た + ら: 'if / when / once', the most flexible conditional: the first thing happens, then the second. Also for discovering something after an action.
Verb-たら + どう (ですか): 'why don't you ~?', a casual suggestion. Can sound pushy toward superiors.
Question word + verb-たら + いいですか: asking for advice, 'what / where / how should I ~?'.
Te form, or noun + で, giving a cause: the first part leads to a feeling or result (sorry I'm late, closed because of the rain). The result is usually not a request or command.
Verb-て + あげる: 'do something for someone', the speaker or their side doing a favor. Can sound condescending toward superiors.
Verb-て + ほしい: 'want someone to do'. The person takes に. ないでほしい is 'I'd rather you didn't'.
Verb-て + いく: a change or action continuing from now into the future, or doing something and then going (will keep growing, take it with you).
Past of ている: 'was doing' at a past moment, or a state that held back then (was living in Osaka).
Verb-て + いただけませんか: a very polite request, 'could I possibly ask you to ~?'. Humbler than てくれませんか.
Verb-て + くれる: someone does a favor for the speaker or the speaker's side. Shows gratitude; the giver is the subject.
Verb-て + くる: a change that has built up to now or is starting to appear (it's getting cold); also 'go and come back / come doing'.
Verb-て + みる: 'try doing' to see what it's like or what happens.
Verb-て + もらう: 'have someone do / get someone to do'. The receiver is the subject and the giver takes に. Humble: ていただく.
Verb-て + おく: do something in advance to prepare, or leave things as they are. Casual: とく.
Verb-て + しまう: the action is done completely, or 'end up doing' with regret or surprise. ちゃう / じゃう is the casual contraction.
Verb-て + すみません: 'sorry for ~', apologizing for something you did or caused (sorry I'm late). More formal: て申し訳ありません.
Verb-て + やる: do something for someone below you (a child, a pet, plants), or a threat like 'I'll show you'. Rougher than てあげる.
Verb-て + よかった: 'I'm glad that ~', relief or happiness about how something turned out.
Verb-ている + ところ: 'right in the middle of doing'. Stresses that the action is in progress at that moment.
Verb or i-adjective て form + も: 'even if / even though', the outcome doesn't change. Nouns and na-adjectives take でも.
Dictionary form + と: 'when / if', a natural or automatic result that always follows (turn right and you'll see it). Can't end with a request or intention.
'You could say / it's fair to call it ~': offers a judgement or a slightly bold description.
A という B: 'a B called A', introducing a name or something the listener may not know. Also reports what something says.
Plain form + ということ: turns a whole statement into a noun, 'the fact that ~', or explains 'what this means is ~'.
'It is said / people say that ~': general belief or common knowledge, without naming a source.
Plain form + と聞いた: 'I heard that ~', reporting something heard, often naming who said it with から or に.
Plain form + と思う: 'I think that ~', giving an opinion or guess. と思っている for a view held over time, or someone else's.
'Things like A and B': lists a few examples casually; works with nouns and verbs. More casual than や〜など.
Dictionary form + ところ: 'about to do', the action is just going to start. The base of a family with ているところ (in the middle) and たところ (just done).
Verb stem + 続ける: 'keep doing / continue', the action goes on without stopping.
Casual と or という: quotes speech or thought (she said she's coming), or marks a topic like は. Very common in conversation.
Passive: ichidan + られる, godan -u to -areru (読まれる). The doer takes に. Also the 'suffering' passive, for something that happens to you and bothers you (got rained on).
Contrast with は: 'A is ..., but B is ...'. Each は marks one side being compared, and が joins the two halves.
Verb stem + やすい: 'easy to do', or 'tends to / is likely to' (breaks easily). Opposite of にくい.
'Finally / at last', after waiting or effort, with relief. For results you wanted.
Noun + より: 'than', the comparison marker on its own (A is bigger than B). In formal notices it also means 'from' a time or place.
Dictionary form or noun + の + 予定だ: 'be scheduled to / plan to', an arranged plan. Firmer than つもり, which is only an intention.
'Seems / appears': a judgement from what you saw, heard or felt. Plain form, noun + の, na-adjective + な. More formal than みたいだ.
'Like / as': ような + noun, ように + verb or adjective, for comparisons and examples (eyes like stars, do it as I showed you). The formal side of みたいな / みたいに.
Dictionary or ない form + ようになる: 'come to / reach the point where', a gradual change in ability or habit (I can read kanji now).
Dictionary or ない form + ようにする: 'make sure to / try to', a conscious effort. ようにしている is something you make a habit of.
Volitional form + と思う: 'I'm thinking of doing'. ようと思っている is an intention held for some time.
'By all means / definitely', with requests and wishes (please do come). Not used with negatives.
With a negative: 'not at all'. Total denial, much stronger than あまり〜ない.
Verb stem + づらい: 'hard to do', mainly because it feels physically or emotionally uncomfortable (hard to say, hard to walk in). More personal than にくい.
Verb stem + 上げる: finish something completely and with care (finish writing a report), or lift up. Not the giving verb あげる.
Dictionary form or noun + の + あまり: 'so much that / out of too much ~', a feeling or state goes so far that an odd or bad result follows. Not あまり〜ない ('not very').
'Far too / so very', an emphatic あまりに. Usually leads to a result: it was so ~ that something happened.
Verb stem + 合う: 'do to each other / together' (help each other, talk it over).
Ba form + いい: 'you just have to / all you need is', simple advice; どうすればいい asks for it. Also a hope: 'it'd be nice if'.
Ba form + よかった: 'should have / I wish I had', regret about the past. With のに it often points at someone else.
'The more ..., the more ...': the same word twice, ば form first, then plain form + ほど (the more I read, the more I understand).
Ba form + いい / よかった + のに: 'if only / it would be better if', regret or a complaint that something isn't happening or didn't happen.
'Only ~ and nothing more': one thing keeps happening while what's expected doesn't, often 〜ばかりで〜ない (all talk and no action).
Plain form or noun + ばかりでなく: 'not only A but also B', with も in the second half. Formal; same idea as だけでなく.
Dictionary form + べきだ: 'should / ought to', what is right or expected. する becomes すべき or するべき.
Dictionary form + べきではない: 'should not', what is wrong or improper. Firmer and more principled than ないほうがいい.
'Not particularly / not really'. Said alone, 別に is a curt 'nothing much'.
Length of time + ぶりに: 'for the first time in ~', doing something again after a gap (met for the first time in five years).
Read ちゅう: 'in the middle of / during' an activity or period (in a meeting, sometime this week). Read じゅう: 'throughout / all over' (all day long, all over the world).
'As much as': verb + だけ for doing something to the full extent (eat as much as you like, できるだけ 'as much as possible'). Beyond the basic だけ, 'only'.
Plain form or noun + だけでなく: 'not only A but also B', followed by も. A little less stiff than ばかりでなく.
'But / however', a casual conjunction to open a sentence or join clauses. Softer than だが; でも is even more casual.
Noun + だらけ: 'full of / covered in' something unwanted (covered in mud, full of mistakes).
'No matter how ~': どんなに + verb or adjective in ても form. The outcome stays the same however much.
'No matter what / at any cost' with a strong wish; with a negative, 'just can't, however hard I try'.
Plain form, noun + の, or adjective + ふりをする: 'pretend to / act as if' (pretend to be asleep).
'Suddenly / without thinking': something happens by chance or for no reason, often a thought or glance (it suddenly struck me).
Verb stem or noun + がち: 'tend to / prone to', mostly for bad habits or conditions (tends to forget, often ill).
Verb stem + がたい: 'hard to / can hardly', for something you can barely bring yourself to accept (unbelievable, unforgivable). Formal.
Verb stem or noun + 気味: 'a touch of / a bit ~', a slight sign of something, usually unwelcome (a slight cold, a bit tired).
Noun or dictionary form + ごとに: 'every / each', something happens at each unit or occasion (every hour, each time it rains).
'To the point that / so ~ that', showing degree (so tired I can't stand). Also a rough amount, 'about'.
A は B ほど〜ない: 'A is not as ~ as B'. Only used with a negative.
'All at once / in one go', many things done at the same time.
'No matter how much ~': いくら + ても form; however much effort or amount, it makes no difference.
Dictionary form + 一方だ: 'keeps on ~ing', a steady change in one direction, often for the worse (prices keep rising).
'What on earth / why on earth', strengthens a question with surprise or annoyance. Used with question words.
Not a real negative: 'isn't it? / don't you think?', seeking agreement or gently reminding (that's nice, isn't it). Softer than じゃないか.
Noun + か何か: 'or something', a vague example (tea or something).
Verb stem + かける: 'half-done / about to', an action started but not finished, or on the verge of happening (a half-read book).
'From A through B': a span of time or area with loose edges, covering the whole stretch between. Vaguer than から〜まで.
Noun + の or plain form + 代わりに: 'instead of', one thing replaces another; also 'in exchange for' (I'll help you, and in return ...).
Verb-た or noun + の + 結果: 'as a result of', the outcome after an action or process.
'In the end / after all', the final outcome, often not what was planned.
'Never / by no means', a strong denial or firm promise.
Verb stem + きれない: 'can't do it all / too much to finish' (can't eat it all, countless). The negative potential of 〜きる.
'Only / just' as a limit (just the two of us). Verb-た + きり: 'since then and nothing more' (left and never came back). Casual: っきり.
Verb stem + きる: do something completely, to the very end (used up all the money, read the whole book).
Sentence-final っけ: 'was it? / did I?', trying to recall something or checking a fact. Casual; often with past forms (だったっけ).
Verb stem + 込む: 'into' (run into, put into), or doing something deeply and thoroughly.
'Precisely / this one above all': stresses the word before it as the one that really counts (this time for sure; I'm the one who should apologize).
Dictionary or ない form + こと ending a sentence: a written rule or instruction, 'must / be sure to'. Common in notices and teachers' directions.
'From the fact that / since': gives the evidence or the origin of a conclusion or name. Formal.
'It's the rule / it's arranged that': a decision or custom already in place. ことになる is the decision being made.
Dictionary form + ことはない: 'there's no need to / don't have to', often reassuring someone.
The same word on both sides of ことは: 'it's true that ~, but ...', a grudging admission before a 'but' (I did read it, but ...).
Degree, 'so ~ that / to the point of' (so happy I could cry); also 'at least' (at least say thanks), or 'nothing is as ~ as' with ない. Beyond the basic 'about' an amount.
Plain form or noun + の + くせに: 'even though / despite', with criticism or contempt for someone's behavior.
'Just like / as if', with ようだ or みたいだ for a vivid comparison that isn't literally true.
'No way / surely not', disbelief that something could happen or be true.
With a negative: 'rarely / hardly ever'.
'Both A and B': adds a second point of the same kind, with ば form in the middle (he can sing and dance too). Used for praise or complaints.
'Maybe / perhaps', a low-confidence guess, often with かもしれない.
'If by any chance', a stronger もし for unlikely or imagined situations.
Noun + 向け: 'made for / aimed at' a target group by design (books for children, products for overseas).
Noun + 向き: 'suited to', it happens to fit that group well (good for beginners); also 'facing' a direction. Unlike 向け, it isn't about who it was made for.
'Rather / if anything', picking the second option as closer to the truth.
'Although / while', contrast between two facts (though small, the room is bright). Formal.
Double negative: 'it's not that I can't / I could, I suppose', a hesitant yes.
ない form + と at the end of a sentence: 'I've got to / have to', short for ないといけない. Casual.
Positive use: 'quite / pretty', better than expected (pretty good). Unlike なかなか〜ない ('not easily').
'Things like / such as', often dismissive or humble (someone like me). なんか and なんて are casual; なんて also shows surprise or disbelief ('to think that ~!').
Verb stem + 直す: 'do again / redo' to fix or improve (rewrite, call back).
'As much as possible / if possible', a reasonable effort.
'Because / the reason is', opens a sentence giving the reason, often ending in からだ.
Plain form + んだって: 'I heard that ~', casual hearsay. As a question: 'is it true that ~?'.
Plain form + に違いない (nouns and na-adjectives drop だ): 'must be / no doubt', a confident conclusion. Stronger and more written than だろう.
Noun + に反して: 'contrary to / against' expectations, plans or rules (contrary to forecasts). に反する + noun.
Noun + にかけて: 'over / through', a stretch of time or area running up to and around that point (through the weekend). Used alone or as the second half of から〜にかけて.
'About / regarding', a formal について. に関する + noun, に関して + verb.
'On behalf of / in place of', one person or thing takes over another's role. More formal than 代わりに.
Noun + に比べて (or と比べて): 'compared with', setting up a comparison between two things. Plain form + のに比べて for actions.
'Get used to': noun + に慣れる; for an action, verb + のに慣れる.
Formal 'in / at' for a place, time or field (in the field of science). における + noun.
'In accordance with' a rule or instruction, or 'as' one change leads to another. Unlike につれて, it also covers following instructions.
'Even if / even granting that', accepting one point while saying something else still holds.
'For / considering', something is different from what you'd expect of it (good Japanese for a beginner).
'Toward / against / in contrast to', marking the target of an action or feeling, or a contrast.
'For / to' someone, from their point of view (important for me).
'About / concerning', the topic of talking, thinking or writing. についての + noun.
'As ~, ...': one gradual change brings another (as it got dark, it grew colder). Not used for following instructions.
Dictionary form + には: 'in order to / to', followed by what's needed or how hard it is. Also 'for' someone's judgement (too hard for me).
'According to', citing a source; the sentence usually ends with そうだ or らしい.
'By / depending on / due to': marks the means, cause, the doer in a passive, or what something varies with. による + noun.
Polite 'I wonder / might it be?', a soft question that sounds less direct than ですか.
Noun + を中心に: 'centered on / mainly around', the core of an activity or area (sales mainly in Asia). を中心とした + noun.
Noun + をはじめ: 'starting with / including', naming the main example first before the rest (Tokyo and other big cities).
Noun + を込めて: 'with / filled with' a feeling put into an action or gift (with love, with thanks).
Noun + を通じて / を通して: 'through / via' a means or go-between (through a friend), or 'throughout' a period (all year round).
Plain form or noun + の + おかげで: 'thanks to', crediting a good result to a cause. Sometimes used sarcastically.
Verb stem + っぱなし: 'left on / left as is', something left in a state it shouldn't be (left the tap running), or going on nonstop.
Noun or verb stem + っぽい: '-ish / -like / tends to'. Casual and often negative (childish, forgetful).
Noun + さえ: 'even', stressing an extreme case (even a child could do it). Often replaces が or を.
さえ + ば form: 'if only / as long as', the one condition that is enough on its own (as long as I have time, ...).
Verb or noun + の + 際に: 'when / on the occasion of', a formal とき for notices, business and announcements.
Verb-ている or noun + の + 最中に: 'right in the middle of', usually when something interrupts (the phone rang mid-meeting).
'Furthermore / even more': adds another point or raises the degree (it got even colder).
'Well then / now', opening a sentence to change the topic or move to the next item.
Plain form or noun + の + せいで: 'because of', blaming a cause for a bad result. The negative counterpart of おかげで.
'At most / at best' (it'll cost a thousand yen at most). Also 'do as much as you can', encouraging or a little ironic.
'For a while', a span that can be short or long. しばらくですね: 'it's been a while'.
Dictionary form + しかない: 'have no choice but to / all I can do is'.
Opens a sentence: 'for that reason' or 'for that purpose', pointing back to what was just said.
'Or', joining two questions to offer a choice (tea, or coffee?). Only in questions; または is the 'or' of statements and forms.
Verb stem + そうもない / そうにない: 'unlikely to / doesn't look like it will' (the rain doesn't look like stopping). The negative of the 'looks like' そうだ.
'Already / by then', a formal or written もう.
'Namely / that is to say', restating something more precisely. Formal and written; つまり is the spoken choice.
Number + counter + は: 'at least', setting a minimum amount (it'll take at least three days).
Verb-た + ものだ: 'used to', fondly recalling something you often did in the past.
Verb-た + とたん (に): 'the moment / just as', something unexpected happens right after. Not for planned follow-up actions.
Dictionary form or noun + の + たびに: 'every time', the same thing happens on each occasion (every time I see this photo, ...).
Dictionary form or noun + の + ために: 'in order to / for' a purpose. After a past form or a cause, it means 'because of'.
'Certainly / it's true', agreeing that something is so, often before a 'but' (true, it's cheap, but ...).
Verb stem + たて: 'freshly / just done' (fresh-baked bread, freshly painted).
たとえ + ても form: 'even if (it were so)', for hypothetical cases; たとえ adds weight to ても.
'For example', introducing an example, often followed by など or とか.
Verb or i-adjective た form + って: 'even if', a casual ても (no matter how much you cry). だって after nouns and na-adjectives.
Verb-て + ばかりいる: 'do nothing but', criticizing someone for always doing one thing (he does nothing but play games).
Verb-て + ごらん: 'try ~ (and see)', said kindly to someone younger, like a child.
Verb-て + はじめて: 'only after ~ did I', a realization that came only after an experience.
Verb-て + からでないと: 'not until / unless you ~ first', followed by something that can't happen yet.

pattern: 〜てしょうがない / 〜てしかたがない
meaning: Te form + しょうがない: 'extremely / can't help feeling', a strong feeling or urge you can't control (so sleepy I can't stand it). しかたがない is a bit more formal.
Verb-て (or noun + で) + 済む: 'get by with / only have to', the matter ends with less trouble or cost than feared. ないで済む: 'get away without having to'.
Verb-て + はいけないから: 'in case / because it would be bad if', the reason for a precaution (take an umbrella in case it rains).
Verb-ている + 場合じゃない: 'this is no time to ~', something more urgent needs doing. ではない in more formal speech.
Noun + 的: '-ic / -al', making a na-adjective (scientific, personal). 的な + noun, 的に + verb.
Verb-ても + 始まらない: 'it's no use ~ing', doing that now won't help (no use crying about it).
Te form + も構わない: 'I don't mind if / it's all right to'. A little more formal than てもいい.

pattern: 〜てもしょうがない / 〜てもしかたがない
meaning: Verb-ても + しょうがない: 'there's no point in ~', it won't change anything. Not the てしょうがない that means 'extremely'.
'Speaking of', picking up a topic just mentioned and saying what it brings to mind (speaking of Kyoto, the temples ...).
Plain form + といい, or た form + らいい: a hope, 'I hope / it'd be nice if' (often with なあ or ですね), or advice, 'you should'.
'Although I say / even though', correcting an impression that's too big (I've been abroad, but only once).
Plain form + ということだ: 'I hear that ~' passing on news, or 'that means ~' drawing a conclusion. Unlike ということ, which only turns a statement into a noun.
'What ~ means is / ~ is' for defining a word, or 'the reason is' when it ends with からだ.
'Speaking of / when you say', recalling an association, or asking for clarification ('by X, do you mean ...?').
Plain form or noun + というより: 'rather than / more ~ than', swapping a description for a more accurate one (more cold than cool).
Plain form + とみえる: 'it seems / apparently', a guess based on visible evidence. とみえて links that guess to what follows.

pattern: 〜とすれば / 〜としたら / 〜とすると
meaning: Plain form + とすれば / としたら / とすると: 'assuming / if it were so', imagining a situation and following it to its result.
Noun or dictionary form + とともに: 'together with', or 'as' one change goes along with another. Formal.
'On the way / partway through'. 途中で for something that happens partway; 途中に for something located along the way.
'By the way', opening a sentence to switch to a new topic.
'However / but then', the result goes against expectations. Not followed by the speaker's own wish or request.
Verb or noun + の + とおりに: 'as / just as', doing something the same way (do it as I said).
Verb stem + 通す: 'do through to the end without stopping' (read it all the way through, hold out).
Noun + として: 'as', in the role or status of (work as an engineer). としては: 'as for / for a ~'.
とても + negative, usually potential: 'can't possibly / by no means', it's beyond you. Not とても 'very'.
Plain form + とは限らない: 'not necessarily / not always', a general rule has exceptions. Often with 必ずしも.
'Without meaning to', doing something by habit or impulse that you shouldn't (I ended up eating too much). Often with てしまう.
'Finally / at last', after a long process; the outcome can be good or bad. やっと stresses relief at a wished-for result.
Verb or noun + の + ついでに: 'while you're at it', doing an extra thing alongside the main one.
'In other words / so', restating or summing up what was said.
Plain form + つもりだった: 'I meant to / I thought I had', when the plan didn't happen or reality turned out different.
Plain form + つもりで: 'with the intention of', or 'as if / acting as though' (treat it as the real test).
Dictionary, ている or ない form, adjective, or noun + の + うちに: 'while still / before it changes', acting while a state lasts (eat it while it's hot).
Verb-た + 上で: 'after (doing), then' (decide after talking it over). Dictionary form or noun + の + 上で: 'when / for the purpose of'.
Plain form or noun + の + 上に: 'on top of / besides', adding a second point of the same kind (cheap and tasty too).
Noun + は別として: 'aside from / setting ~ apart', putting one point aside to talk about the rest.
A はもちろん B も: 'not to mention A, B too', giving the obvious case before a less obvious one.
A は B で有名だ: 'A is famous for B'. で marks what it's known for.
Plain form + わけだ: 'that's why / no wonder / so that means', a natural conclusion from what's known.
Plain form + わけではない: 'it's not that / it doesn't mean that', denying only part of something.
Plain form + わけがない: 'there's no way that', a firm denial based on reasoning. Close to はずがない.
Dictionary form + わけにはいかない: 'can't (afford to)', ruled out by social, moral or practical reasons even though it's possible.
Plain form or noun + の + わりに: 'considering / for', the result is more or less than you'd expect (cheap for the quality).
'On purpose / deliberately', often for something mean or surprising.
'Go to the trouble of / specially', an effort beyond what's needed, often for someone else (thanks for coming all this way).
Noun + よりも: 'than', a more emphatic より; 何よりも means 'more than anything'.
Verb stem + ようがない: 'there's no way to', no method exists (there's no way to contact him).
Plain form or noun + の + ような気がする: 'I have a feeling that / it seems to me', a vague impression.
Dictionary or ない form + ように: 'so that / in order that', for goals you can't directly control (so I don't forget); also reported requests and wishes (told him to come early).
Plain form or noun + の + ように見える: 'looks like / seems', a judgement from appearance. Takes a whole clause, where に見える takes a noun or adjective.
Volitional form + としない: 'won't even try to / refuses to', about someone else's unwillingness.
Volitional form + とする: 'try to' (an attempt, often unsuccessful) or 'be about to' (just as I was leaving).
ない stem + ずに: 'without doing', more formal than ないで. する becomes せずに.
ない stem + ずにはいられない: 'can't help doing', an urge you can't hold back. する becomes せずには.
Number or amount + ずつ: 'each / at a time' (two each, little by little).
